question: What is the primary function of mucus in the gastrointestinal tract?

options.A: Stimulating the production of gastric acid
options.B: Protecting the epithelial lining from abrasion
options.C: Lowering the pH of the intestinal lumen
options.D: Absorbing digested fats into the bloodstream

explanation: Mucus forms a viscous, protective coat that prevents mechanical damage and chemical injury to the delicate gut lining. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h1)

question: Why does the digestive tract secrete large volumes of fluid daily?

options.A: To provide a medium for enzymatic reactions and movement
options.B: To maintain high blood pressure throughout the body
options.C: To cool down the internal temperature of the abdomen
options.D: To excrete heavy metals and metabolic waste products

explanation: A fluid environment is essential for dissolving nutrients and allowing digestive enzymes to freely interact with food particles. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h1)

question: Which enzyme is responsible for the initial breakdown of starch in the mouth?
explanation: Salivary amylase is secreted by the salivary glands to start splitting complex starches into simpler sugars right inside the oral cavity. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h2)

question: What stops the action of salivary amylase once food reaches the stomach?

options.A: The absence of water in the gastric contents
options.B: The immediate absorption of the enzyme by the stomach wall
options.C: The highly acidic environment of the stomach
options.D: The presence of bile acids mixed with the food bolus

explanation: Hydrochloric acid in the stomach lowers the pH significantly, causing salivary amylase to denature and lose its catalytic activity. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h2)

question: Which gastric cells secrete hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor?
explanation: Parietal cells in the gastric glands are responsible for producing both hydrochloric acid and the intrinsic factor needed for vitamin B12 uptake. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h3)

question: Why is pepsin secreted in an inactive form called pepsinogen?

options.A: To delay carbohydrate breakdown until food enters the large intestine
options.B: To ensure it only works when mixed with bile salts in the duodenum
options.C: To allow it to travel safely through the bloodstream without reacting
options.D: To prevent it from digesting the protein structures of the cells that make it

explanation: Enzymes that digest protein are synthesized as inactive precursors to protect the producing cells from self-destruction. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of the bicarbonate secreted by pancreatic duct cells?

options.A: Stimulating the release of bile from the gallbladder
options.B: Neutralizing acidic chyme coming from the stomach
options.C: Emulsifying large fat droplets into smaller micelles
options.D: Activating salivary amylase in the oral cavity

explanation: Bicarbonate provides an alkaline buffer that raises the pH of the intestinal contents, protecting the mucosa and creating an optimal environment for pancreatic enzymes. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h4)

question: A patient lacks functional pancreatic lipase. Which nutrient group will show impaired digestion?
explanation: Pancreatic lipase is the primary enzyme responsible for breaking down dietary triglycerides into absorbable fatty acids and monoglycerides. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h4)

question: Where is bile primarily stored and concentrated before being released into the intestine?
explanation: The gallbladder acts as a reservoir that stores and concentrates liver bile until it is needed for fat digestion. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h5)

question: How do bile salts assist in the digestion of dietary lipids?

options.A: By increasing the acidity of the chyme in the duodenum
options.B: By chemically converting fatty acids directly into amino acids
options.C: By acting as an enzyme that digests triglycerides into sugars
options.D: By breaking large fat droplets into smaller emulsified particles

explanation: Bile salts have hydrophobic and hydrophilic ends that reduce surface tension, breaking big fat globs into tiny droplets to expose more surface area. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h5)

question: Where are brush-border enzymes like maltase and lactase typically located?

options.A: Attached to the microvilli of the small intestine
options.B: Secreted directly by the acinar cells of the pancreas
options.C: Freely floating in the acidic fluid of the stomach
options.D: Stored inside the hepatocytes of the liver

explanation: Brush-border enzymes are anchored to the plasma membrane of the microvilli in the small intestine to complete the final breakdown of nutrients. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h6)

question: What is the functional advantage of having enzymes located on the brush border rather than free in the lumen?

options.A: It stops bacteria in the large intestine from consuming the food
options.B: It ensures final digestion happens right at the site of absorption
options.C: It allows the stomach to reuse the enzymes repeatedly
options.D: It prevents the enzymes from ever coming into contact with water

explanation: Keeping the final digestive enzymes anchored at the absorption surface allows immediate transport of the resulting small molecules into the enterocytes. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h6)

question: Which cranial nerve plays a major role in parasympathetic stimulation of digestive secretions?
explanation: The vagus nerve carries parasympathetic signals that promote digestive tract motility and glandular secretion. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h7)

question: What is the primary stimulus for the release of secretin from the duodenal mucosa?

options.A: The complete absence of food in the digestive tract
options.B: The presence of large protein chunks in the mouth
options.C: The arrival of acidic chyme from the stomach
options.D: The mechanical stretching of the empty stomach wall

explanation: Secretin is released in response to low pH levels in the duodenum to signal the pancreas for bicarbonate-rich fluid neutralization. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h7)

question: Pernicious anemia is directly linked to a deficiency in which gastric factor?
explanation: Intrinsic factor is required for vitamin B12 absorption in the ileum; without it, patients develop pernicious anemia. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h8)

question: Why does a deficiency in lactase enzyme cause diarrhea and abdominal cramping?

options.A: The liver stops making bile salts, which halts all fat digestion completely
options.B: Undigested lactose creates an osmotic load and undergoes bacterial fermentation
options.C: The stomach responds by producing excess hydrochloric acid to burn the sugar
options.D: Pancreatic enzymes overreact and attack the walls of the large intestine

explanation: Unabsorbed lactose draws water into the bowel lumen through osmosis and is fermented by gut bacteria, producing gas, pain, and diarrhea. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h8)
